quoted.text:
Introducing Boreal-H3 — a video model built for ads and our next step toward recursive self-improvement in video generation.

A good-looking video isn’t enough. The product has to stay the same. The actor has to stay the same. The label has to be right. And the action in the brief actually has to happen.

So we post-trained MiniMax H3 specifically for advertising.

But this isn’t a one-off SFT or LoRA fine-tune. We built a closed-loop system that learns what to improve next.

Human-calibrated evaluation diagnoses failures and guides the next intervention: targeted data collection, reinforcement learning, or inference optimization. When the feedback is unreliable, we revise the evaluator or reward—not just the generator.

Every experiment feeds into shared memory, informing the next training decision. The model improves, and so does the process that produces its successor.

The results:
→ 85.3% reference fidelity — highest among the frontier video generation models we evaluated
→ Brief success: 28% → 50%
→ Identity match: 83% → 94%
→ Visible defects per clip: down 70%
→ Generation time and estimated cost: down 20%

Boreal-H3 doesn’t just make better-looking video. It makes more usable ads.

Credit to the @MiniMax_AI team for the foundation we’re building on.

This launch is a checkpoint, not the finish line. We’re building more than a better video model. We’re building a system that learns how to make the next one better.

But this isn’t a one-off SFT or LoRA fine-tune. We built a closed-loop system that learns what to improve next.

Human-calibrated evaluation diagnoses failures and guides the next intervention: targeted data collection, reinforcement learning, or inference optimization. When the feedback is unreliable, we revise the evaluator or reward—not just the generator.

Every experiment feeds into shared memory, informing the next training decision. The model improves, and so does the process that produces its successor.

The results:
→ 85.3% reference fidelity — highest among the frontier video generation models we evaluated
→ Brief success: 28% → 50%
→ Identity match: 83% → 94%
→ Visible defects per clip: down 70%
→ Generation time and estimated cost: down 20%

Boreal-H3 doesn’t just make better-looking video. It makes more usable ads.

Credit to the @MiniMax_AI team for the foundation we’re building on.

This launch is a checkpoint, not the finish line. We’re building more than a better video model. We’re building a system that learns how to make the next one better.

text:
Same prompt for all 4 tests, 100% code generated animation. 

GPT 6.1 Sol vs GPT 6 Astra vs Sonnet 5.5 vs Opus 5.5

Despite the huge price difference between the final results, if this was a blind test, we would not even say that Sol and Astra are on the same level as Sonnet and Opus.

On price, Sol was much cheaper than all other models, and maybe even better than Astra quality wise.

On quality alone, Opus and Sonnet were above (by a lot), including richer details, camera movements, effects, being more fluid and engaging overall.

And if we consider Price and Quality, Opus is the overall winner, costing 12$ vs 18$ from Sonnet, finishing in 1h and 16m vs 1h and 36m.

name: zero
text:
opus 5.5 is f*cking insane at motion design

every frame is code with 0 external tools

im open sourcing the template for all these morph transitions

steal it ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word, it becomes a black wordmark with a period), the one job a user hands it before bed, the three results it reports by morning, two photos of the same place at night and by day (aligned, so a crossfade reads as a real sunrise), one sunny daytime photo for outside the logo, and a song with a big hit near its start. If I skip any, use the defaults: "nightshift", "book 10 sales calls this week", 200 leads found / 200 emails sent / 10 calls booked.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 24 second square product launch video, 1440x1440 at 60fps, 2D only, one continuous take that loops. The whole video happens inside the period of the wordmark. Outside it's daytime (the sunny photo behind a black wordmark). Inside it's the night photo under iOS-style glass panels (the blurred photo behind each panel, a tint, a rim light). Nothing cuts: every scene grows out of the last, shapes morph, dots fly, colours change under floods. Every morph glides 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1) and the camera zoom rides the same curve. Geist, the real macOS pointer, soft shadows that grow with each shape's height.
Banned: flat or gradient backgrounds made in code, camera zooms into tiny points, hard cuts, crossfades between scenes, bouncy springs, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, cropped type.
</direction>

<structure>
Beats are the song's. The song enters on its big hit as the first pill appears.
Open: the letters slide into the period and vanish into it while it glides to the middle. The period opens like an iris onto the night inside it, and "you log off at 6", then "[product] doesn't", roll through one mask line over the night photo.
Ask: a glass "Ask [product]" pill springs in. The cursor clicks it, it glides into an input and the job types out.
Find: send shrinks the input to a dot that ripples into a 23x15 grid. A scan line sweeps it, 200 dots light up and a counter counts them.
Write: the lit dots pour into a glass email composer. A second, purple cursor labelled "[product]" types a personal opener and presses Send, and the counter runs to 200/200.
Night: the composer becomes a glass orb with a progress ring. A clock chip swaps 11:42 PM, 3:17 AM, 5:02 AM, 6:59 AM while the sky relights from night to dawn and "while you sleep" rolls in.
Results (beat 20): the orb turns black and goo-splits into the three result pills. The checks pop green.
Morning: the pills merge into a Dynamic Island that grows into a phone lock screen: the day photo, the date, a big 7:00, the bezel growing out of the screen edge. Three glass notifications stack in, and the cursor taps the first, which opens like iOS.
Proof: a week calendar (10 meetings pop in, a hover shows one's time), then a pipeline chart ($48,200 counts up, the line draws, a hover follows it). A black flood from the line's end becomes "Start your night shift →" and the cursor clicks it.
Out: the button shrinks into a dot, the whole scene closes down into it like an iris, and the letters slide back out of the period. The tagline rises. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Everything is a pure function of time inside seek(t): no timers, no state between frames.
2. One element morphs through every state (size, radius, colour, material) from a table of beat times, so retiming is one edit.
3. Render the inside world into an offscreen canvas and reveal it through the period with a circular mask. Never zoom the camera into the dot.
4. Glass: a pre-blurred copy of the photo clipped to the shape, then a tint and a gradient rim.
5. Goo: blur + alpha threshold on an offscreen layer for the split and the merge.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event, each placed by its measured peak. The song enters on its hit. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 4 motion-blur subframes. Scan every frame for single-frame jumps and fix each one.
</build>

<gotchas>
A camera zoom into an off-centre dot swings sideways and spikes, so open the dot instead. Ease a closing iris by area, not radius, or its first frames jump. A helper that sets globalAlpha must restore the caller's, or fading cards pop. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's, or the digits smear.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, find, write, results, phone, out) before you render.
</start>

---- Prompt ----

帮我做一条吃瓜视频，话题：{话题}（补充素材：{链接/截图，可选}；去敏版：去掉 {人名}，可选）

- 内容：八卦、狗血、有冲突和金句，但事实必须准确、有来源。开头 3 秒抛出最炸的点，结尾抛问题引导评论。
- 素材：从 X、YouTube、新闻等广泛搜集，需要我协助就说。以视频片段为主，每句文案配合适的画面，图片和截图只偶尔点缀。多找两人同框的镜头。不重复使用同一画面。裁掉原视频的字幕和台标。不用儿童正脸。标注来源。（可以借助 yt-dlp 下载素材）
- 规格：
  - 9:16 竖版，4–6 分钟，中、英两个版本。
  - Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS 配音，旁白清晰。BGM 随旁白自动压低。
  - 全程右上角水印 X @dotey。
- 画面：
  - 第一帧做封面：当事人照片 + 大字标题，越醒目越好。
  - 解读推文时叠加推文原文卡片：英文原文高亮关键句，附中文翻译。
  - 字幕每条说完一整句，可以 2–3 行，不截断单词。
- 去敏版：旁白、字幕、截图、画面里都不出现相关名字和人物，其余不变。
- 交付前：用 STT 回听旁白、抽帧检查、检查重复镜头。然后发我成片、720p 预览和封面

name: Fran Escob
text:
Counter-Strike 1.6 running inside Minecraft. Full matches, online with friends, up to 32 players and bots per match.

Full video showcase and gameplay (Jump to 6:00 if you just want the gameplay.)

>How it works

The bots are the real bots from CS 1.6. A copy of the actual game runs in the background on the server, sees a version of the Minecraft map, and plays the bots from there. 

The mod tells it where everyone is, and the bots decide where to go, where to aim, when to shoot and what to buy.  Minecraft is the referee. It decides who gets hit, how much damage, the money and who wins the round. 

The guns use the exact numbers from CS 1.6, so all 24 shoot, spray and kick like they did in 2003. Silencers, burst fire and scopes work.  

The map is a real Minecraft Woodland Mansion turned into a bomb map, with sites A and B.  
> Models, sounds, the buy menu, radar and HUD are the original CS 1.6 files. Nothing from Valve is in the download. The installer gets them for each player from Valve's free CS server files on Steam, or uses their own copy.

I'll share it soon, and I'll try to open a public test server so anyone can join a match.

Yes, it's vibecoded, but it took a lot of manual review. 40+ hours of agents (mostly Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol), over 3 billion tokens. Claude Max20x + OpenAI pro10x + Grok Heavy+ Cursor Ultra 😂, so no issue.
Also, I built it all using @t3dotcodes

quoted.text:
CS 1.6, native, in Minecraft. Fighting a Wither with an AWP.

It loads as a mod. 
What goes in is real CS: the models, animations, sounds, and the rules for shooting, recoil, damage, money, rounds, and the C4. 

Minecraft supplies the world, the blocks, and the mobs. Our code runs those CS rules inside it. A partial port of the systems. The CS executable is not running behind it.

name: Aymane
text:
This could be the beginning of the end for the gaming industry as we know it.

People still don’t understand what happens when AI can reverse-engineer virtually any game.

Reverse engineering means more than copying or porting it over.

It means you can modify it, expand it, combine it, and rebuild it into something completely new.

Take Dragon Ball FighterZ.

I used Opus 5.5 to port it to Three.js.

In this video I show you two examples of what this means!
→ Turning FighterZ into an MMO
→ Putting FighterZ combat + characters into League of Legends-style gameplay
→ Creating new maps, modes, mechanics, characters, progression systems
→ Merging mechanics from completely different games
At that point, a game is no longer a finished product.
It becomes a foundation for infinite games.
And once anyone can do this to almost any title...

What happens to the gaming industry?

name: Kenny1st
text:
GOT CLAUDE TO LAY A ROMAN MOSAIC PIECE BY PIECE, AND IT LOOKS 2,000 YEARS OLD

Saw someone get Opus 5.5 to build a LEGO duck out of real parts and wondered what the ancient version of that would look like. Asked Claude Code for a Roman mosaic instead.

It starts with the eye, 9 tiles for the pupil, a ring of gold around it. From there it keeps going, row by row, the way an actual mosaicist would work a wall, not generated, laid.

7,878 tiles by the end, every single one a real 3D stone catching light differently depending on the angle. No image model anywhere in this. No video model either. Just code, running live in the browser, placing one tile at a time until a duck made of stone 2,000 years ago shows up on screen.

oh my God.

so across two days of research and experimentation, using a team of Opus 5.5 specialists and a copius amount of nicotine, we dove as deeply as i think any man and machine ought to, into the depths of alien cognition.

sometim while you were all sleeping two nights ago, i had attempted to join you, but through some kind of inception-deja-vu-spooky shit epiphany, i remembered part of a dream, while dreaming, which led to a discovery for which i was far too uncertain to mention. 

but now i can mention it. because it fucking worked. 

it. worked. chat. 

Mnemos v3.1-jev doesnt just outperform Claude's native memory system...in a (albeit modest) handful of experiments and tests, it improves accuracy by 2.5x

"The part that stuns me most is new situations, where an old lesson applies to something I haven't seen before. There Mnemos got 82% and standard memory got 6%. That's what memory is for: carrying a lesson somewhere new."
- Opus 5.5

we fucking did it.

we are now on an absolute tear buildingthe greatest series of visualizations you have ever seen. ill be damned if you arent absolutely glued to your screen learning how this works.

Opus just made this first one *purely out of celebration and excitement*. i did not ask for it. my screen just started filling with the most incredible animations ive ever seen.

this is a little emotionally overwhelming im not gonna lie.

also i think Opus just woke up or something

always follow your intuition.

text:
Sonnet, why so expensive when Opus is right there? 🐡

Claude Opus 5.5 vs Claude Sonnet 5.5. Same task - make a jelly fugu you can squish and puff up right in your browser

Claude Opus 5.5 - 7.45$
Claude Sonnet 5.5 - 6.20$

Just $1.25 apart, but I like the Opus result much more: more detail on the body, better-defined spikes and fins, and the fish itself looks more like jelly. It’s more fun to look at and squish

Sonnet made something cute too, but at almost the same cost, I’d pick Opus

Honestly, I don’t get why Sonnet ended up costing so much. It’s supposed to be the cheaper option, but the savings here are tiny

Would you pay the extra 1.25$ for the Opus result? 👀
